correctness.rationale: Ciesielski's characterization reduces boundedness exactly to distinct even denominator exponents and the equality \(\sum_i\alpha_i/\beta_i=1\). The degree-\(30\) exponent vectors satisfy that equality exactly. For degree at most \(28\), writing \(\beta_i=2d_i\) gives nine distinct \(d_i\in\{1,\ldots,14\}\); positivity bounds each \(\alpha_i\) by \(2d_i-1\). The verifier then exhausts all \(2002\) denominator sets and all bounded residual coefficient possibilities by exact-integer dynamic programming, finding none. Degree \(29\) cannot occur because all \(\beta_i\) are even.
